localBiteReport: Reports from the Choctawhatchee Bay / Destin area this week reflect post-Hurricane Isaias recovery conditions across the Emerald Coast, with water clarity and fishing activity varying by location. The most recent regional report (October 16–22) notes that calm, sunny weather returned quickly after the storm, but dirty or stained water is affecting some areas; surf anglers near Pensacola and Navarre were already finding black drum, redfish, and pompano biting, and a similar pattern is expected to hold for Choctawhatchee Bay as conditions settle. Earlier in the month (approximately two weeks ago), guides reported that redfish and speckled trout were heating up in the bayous of Choctawhatchee Bay — a pattern typical for the fall Destin Fishing Rodeo period. Water temperature at this location today is 77°F. Overall, fall inshore bay species — redfish, trout, sheepshead around structure, and flounder — are entering one of their stronger seasonal windows, though post-storm water clarity may require anglers to adjust presentations and location.
